summary: # Pressure Map Improvements For Garment Fit | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe, and I'm going to show you this great update we have with our fitting maps. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Accessing Fit Maps Here, I've got my avatar with some garments on her, and I definitely want to check out this fit. If you want to check out a fit, there are many ways to do that, but some of the best tools we have are these fit maps. To find them, navigate to your 3D toggle menu located over here. Right below the fabric garment rendering style, you will find the fit maps. ## Fit Map Options You have a few different fit map options available: - **Stress** - **Strain** - **Fit** - **Pressure** ### Using the Pressure Map The pressure map is particularly useful because it shows the pressure exerted on the avatar. Just make sure to simulate first before you access the pressure map. A pop-up window will remind you if you forget, but I remembered, so I ensured I simulated. Once simulated, I can turn on my pressure map. What this feature does is indicate where the most pressure is applied on my avatar, highlighting the areas where she would feel the garment the most. ## Interacting with the Pressure Map To check the pressure values, hold down the control key. This will allow you to see the pressure data right next to your cursor. You can simply use your right mouse button to click, and you will see the pressure values displayed. Even if you click on areas with no pressure, it will show a value of zero. This means you will always receive some information. You can click to see exactly how much pressure is being applied to our avatar from the garment. ## Understanding Pressure Values I want to remind everyone that colors can sometimes be deceiving. Red isn't always bad, and blue isn't always good; it all depends on the garment you’re fitting. For this athleisure garment, honestly, it looks pretty good. Having red in certain areas probably just means that the elastic is functioning properly, and that is a good sign. ### Final Thoughts Again, red isn't always bad, and blue isn't always good; it all depends on the garment you’re fitting. Use your own judgment when interpreting these colors. Thanks so much for watching! If you have any questions, check out the comment section below, and someone will get back to you. Don't forget to check out the rest of our videos on YouTube; we've got so many of them! I'll see you in the next one. Bye-bye! And don't forget to like and subscribe while you're at it. Thanks again so much, and keep having fun in Clo!
